findings.text: In a context WITHOUT the Promise intrinsic, merely creating an async function or async generator object leaks a GC object; QuickJS then fails assert(list_empty(&rt->gc_obj_list)) in JS_FreeRuntime and the PROCESS ABORTS (STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN in the debug build). Bisected with 7+4 probes (probe commits 409e19e, 1d886fc). Mitigation: Promise intrinsic added (probe shows no leak), global Promise deleted, jobs never executed. Consequence: an in-process native engine can take down the host on hostile source; the worker-process lane is MANDATORY before production use, not optional hardening.

Scripts that never reach an engine poll (about every 10,000 branch/call steps) cost 0 provider units; long C builtins and parsing are not interruptible in-process. Matches EXPR-PROVIDER-04: needs worker deadline.
QuickJS out-of-memory is a catchable InternalError; heap stays bounded by the limit but script can swallow the error and continue.

Without JS_AddIntrinsicEval even the embedder cannot compile source (JS_EvalInternal throws), so no trusted-compile-realm split is possible through the safe wrapper; only the name/constructor hardening above is available. Completeness of denial is NOT_PROVEN.

CONFIRMED and fixed: classify read name/message/stack of the thrown value through user accessors after the interrupt had been disarmed (a looping getter = unbounded hang); Object.defineProperty in the extractor also read Object.prototype.get/set through the prototype chain. Both paths now run no user code and the interrupt stays armed to the end of the session. In worker mode the host wall-clock kill additionally bounds any residual hang.

CONFIRMED and fixed: a thrown Error with name 'InternalError' mapped to EngineFailure::Internal and poisoned the provider permanently. Interrupts now come from handler state and adapter failures from rquickjs error types; thrown-value kind comes from captured intrinsic prototype identity. RESIDUAL BY DESIGN: message-derived classes stay forgeable by scripts (new RangeError('Maximum call stack') -> Budget stack, new InternalError('out of memory') -> Budget memory, TypeError with the unavailable marker -> Unsupported); the effect is a typed budget denial for that script only, no poison, hang or state change. [SUPERSEDED by R5 ffe5592: no message text selects a class; QuickJS stack/heap limit errors are Thrown -> Unsupported; Budget only from interrupt state and rquickjs Error::Allocation; see notes.remediation_R5]

On Windows an aborted worker (exit code -1073740791) stays alive about 5 s because Windows Error Reporting (WerFault.exe) handles the crash before the process exits. Without unsafe FFI (SetErrorMode) the host cannot suppress this, so a crash is reported as engine_crashed only when the process exits within the evaluation deadline; a worker still alive at deadline+grace is killed and reported as a deadline denial. The real-abort reproducer therefore runs with the 10 s deadline ceiling; respawn bounds use an immediate-exit fault. WerFault showed no window handle on this machine; WER UI behaviour on other systems is NOT_PROVEN.

The slice-2 Promise-intrinsic mitigation removes the abort from hardened contexts, so the reproducer needs the worker test fault WorkerTestFault::AsyncAbort (worker reads env HSK_MOTION_JS_WORKER_TEST_FAULT): sources containing 'async' then run in the unmitigated context (no Promise, no bootstrap) and trip the real QuickJS gc_obj_list assert at runtime free. ExitMidRequest and DeafInterrupt are likewise worker-env test knobs; the host never sets them in production.

In bundled QuickJS-NG 0.16.2, Error stack is an Error.prototype accessor over [[ErrorData]] and Error.prepareStackTrace is honoured when an error is created; that user hook runs at throw time under the armed interrupt. The describer reads stack only through the captured native getter and accepts string primitives only.

Found under CPU load during the crash test: starting a worker inside the 250 ms default deadline produced spurious deadline denials. Fixed by measuring setup time and granting it back to the host deadline (HostBridge::grant_time, default no-op).

NOT_PROVEN: operating-system memory/CPU caps for the worker (Windows Job Object) and crash-reporter suppression need unsafe FFI, which the crate forbids and this lane was told not to add. Enforced instead: engine heap limit with readback inside the worker, wall-clock kill, cancel kill, bounded respawn.

MEASURED (os_caps test data run): with a 400 ms CPU allowance armed through JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_PROCESS_TIME alone, a `while (true) {}` worker was stopped by the kernel after 3.77 s, and two 1.1 s requests ran past an absolute 400 ms limit. The host therefore polls the job's own user+kernel accounting every 5 ms (408-422 ms measured) and keeps the kernel limit only as a backstop.

Five consecutive swallowed allocation bombs (cap 96 MiB, engine heap limit 512 MiB) were each reported as Budget(Memory) from JOB_OBJECT_MSG_PROCESS_MEMORY_LIMIT; no lost-notice race was observed. Microsoft documents these completion-port messages as notifications without a delivery guarantee, so a missed notice would leave the earlier classification (Unsupported/engine_crashed), never a false budget.

JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_DIE_ON_UNHANDLED_EXCEPTION alone did not shorten the hold of an aborted worker (MSVC abort() path, WerFault.exe observed, 2 s to past 10 s). FIXED by the worker calling SetErrorMode(SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS | SEM_NOGPFAULTERRORBOX | SEM_NOOPENFILEERRORBOX) and _set_abort_behavior(0, _WRITE_ABORT_MSG | _CALL_REPORTFAULT) at start: abort() then ends the process with exit code 3 (Microsoft Learn: with _CALL_REPORTFAULT clear and no reporter, abort calls _exit, exit code 3), 10 of 10 strict runs in 1-2 s. UNVERIFIED: which of the two calls alone suffices (not isolated); non-abort faults such as an access violation are covered only by SetErrorMode as documented and are not tested; WerSetFlags/WerAddExcludedApplication were not needed and not used.

decisions.text: rquickjs Function::new requires 'js-lifetime closures, so a borrowed &mut HostBridge cannot be captured; avoided unsafe lifetime erasure with deterministic miss/replay (crate keeps forbid(unsafe_code)).
ScriptedEngine interprets fixed command words only and must never grow into a JS evaluator.
MOT-259 has no runtime-error code: thrown reference error -> ReferenceMissing, other thrown -> Unsupported (UNVERIFIED mapping).
motion-js-es2018@1 is a working identifier, not from the spec.
Wall-clock deadline is a cooperative resource guard; the deterministic budget is Fuel. Both surface as Budget; kind only visible in ProviderStats denial counters.
A Budget error returned by HostRead is mapped to BudgetKind::Fuel and cannot be caught by script code.
Motion has no engine-fault code: EngineFailure::Faulted maps to ExprErrorCode::Unsupported with the typed cause in ProviderStats::faulted (UNVERIFIED mapping); the provider is not poisoned.

QuickJsEngine is crate-private; the in-process path is reachable only as QuickJsOptions::unsafe_in_process(). Existing contract tests run in-process by default and against the worker with HSK_MOTION_JS_TEST_BACKEND=worker.
Worker process start is host setup, not script time: the script keeps the budget left before checkout and the host deadline is extended by the measured setup time.

diagnosis.cause: profile validator accepted a raw U+0000 inside string literals and comments; rquickjs fails CString::new(src) before the engine runs (Error::InvalidString); quickjs.rs classify mapped every non-exception wrapper error to EngineFailure::Internal; provider.rs map_failure poisons on Internal (sticky)
diagnosis.engine_evidence: rquickjs-core-0.14.0 src/context/ctx.rs:144 (eval_raw: CString::new(src)? -> Error::InvalidString, the only source-derived site on the eval path; :187 CString::new(filename) is the constant 'expr'); src/result.rs:78 (InvalidString(NulError)), :502 (From<NulError>); JS_Eval itself takes input_len (rquickjs-sys-0.14.0 quickjs/quickjs.c:38316-38326) so the engine could parse a NUL, the wrapper refuses first. Other code points: &str is valid UTF-8 so no lone surrogates or overlong forms reach the wrapper; no other code point produces InvalidString or any other non-exception error on this path (Error::Exception from JS_Eval is a thrown value handled by the describer).
diagnosis.why_third_fail_class: same outcome as R3 and R5 (script input -> Internal -> sticky poison) by a route no test covered
